title: Universal-section map from free-representable derived Hom to cohomology
statement: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $W\to X$ an object of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $F$ an abelian sheaf on $Y$, and $q\in\mathbf N$. Set $T=Y\times_X W$ and $r:T\to Y$. Let $A=h^*\mathbf Z[W]$, where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the free represented sheaf is obtained by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Its universal section on $T$ is obtained by evaluating the inverse image/direct image adjunction unit at the identity of $W$, changing the pullback factor order and restricting to the final object of $T_{et}$. The constant-sheaf adjunction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] turns it into $\gamma:\mathbf Z_T\to r^*A$. Define $C_{h,F,q,W}$ by converting $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(Y)}(A[0],F[0][q])$ to $\operatorname{Ext}^q(A,F)$ through the fully faithful inclusion [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], applying the exact functor $r^*$ and precomposing with $\gamma$. Its target is $H^q(T,r^*F)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For $F=\mathbf Z/e_Y$, define the cyclic map by composing with the canonical constant-coefficient pullback isomorphism on cohomology.

mathlib_searches.query: Cohomology of a sheaf restricted to an etale object is Ext from the free abelian sheaf on the representable
Derived Hom from the free abelian sheaf on an etale representable computes cohomology of the restricted sheaf naturally under restriction
Ext of a free abelian representable sheaf equals derived evaluation on a localized site; CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext, Function.Bijective; mapExtUnit|extAddEquiv|uliftYonedaEquiv
mathlib_searches.results: LeanFinder returns Sheaf.H, cohomologyPresheafFunctor and generic Ext/resolution APIs; Loogle returns mk₀_bijective and mapExt bijections, not representable-restriction comparison. Local source reading finds the general free-sheaf and sections constructions in EtaleOpenCohomologyComparison and the exact Ext adjunction in MapBijective; the former are reused. Open-object cohomology comparison requires an open immersion and does not apply to a general etale W. The latter still needs the representable isomorphism and identification of its unit with the explicit generator.
mathlib_searches.verdict: reuse existing constructions; neither remaining theorem is an existing declaration
